# Entire Upgrade

An [Entire CLI](https://github.com/entireio/cli) plugin that upgrades the system-installed `entire` binary.

This plugin builds a binary named `entire-upgrade`, which is invoked as:

```sh
entire upgrade
```

By default it checks the stable release channel and installs only when the
latest stable build is newer than the current binary. Use `--nightly` to opt
into the latest nightly build:

```sh
entire upgrade --nightly
```

If you are running a nightly build and want to move back to the latest stable
release, use:

```sh
entire upgrade --stable
```

The plugin detects whether the active `entire` binary was installed through
Homebrew, `install.sh`, or `go install`, then runs the matching updater. Each
release ships both `entire` and `git-remote-entire`, and the upgrade replaces
both. The Homebrew and `install.sh` paths unpack the two binaries together; the
`go install` path builds and installs each one beside the existing `entire`.

## Installation

```sh
git clone https://github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade.git
cd entire-upgrade
mise build
entire plugin install ./entire-upgrade --force
```

## Development

This project uses [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) for task automation and dependency management.

### Prerequisites

- [mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/) - Install with `curl https://mise.run | sh`

### Getting Started

===CMD DIRS===
entire-upgrade
./cmd/entire-upgrade/main.go
===go.mod module===
module github.com/entireio/entire-upgrade

content.text:
## Bottom line

**The bug isn't in the install code you changed — it's the early-return gate above it.** `entire upgrade` decides "already up to date" by looking at the `entire` binary's version *only*. When `entire` is already current, it `return nil` before `Install` is ever called, so `git-remote-entire` never gets touched. Your `installWithGo` change is correct, but it only runs on the path that never executed.

The offending code (`internal/upgrade/run.go:96-101`):

```go
compare := latest.Compare(install.Version)        // <- only entire's version
channelSwitch := opts.ExplicitChannel && !installationMatchesChannel(install, channel)
if compare <= 0 && !channelSwitch {
    fmt.Fprintf(stdout, "Entire CLI is already up to date for the %s channel.\n", channel)
    return nil                                     // <- bails before installing git-remote-entire
}
```

Your run hit exactly this: `entire` was at the latest nightly → `compare <= 0` → "already up to date" → returned without ever installing the helper.

## What I confirmed

- `git-remote-entire` has **no `--version`** — it's a git remote helper (`usage: git-remote-entire <remote-name> <url>`). So we can't version-check it the way we do `entire`.
- It **does** embed the `github.com/entireio/cli` module version in Go build info (currently `v0.7.3`), readable via the same `versionFromGoBuildInfo` the code already uses as the go-install fallback. That's our version signal for the helper across the board.
- Right now both your binaries are at `v0.7.3` and timestamped 09:25 today — so something (a later manual install) did sync them after the 09:16 paste. The code path is still broken regardless.

## Plan to handle both binaries independently

1. **Detect the helper independently.** Add detection for `git-remote-entire` beside `entire` (same dir as `install.BinaryPath`): present? what version (via build info)?
2. **Gate on the set, not just `entire`.** Print "already up to date" only when *both* binaries are current. If the helper is missing or behind `latest`, proceed even when `entire` is current.
3. **Install per-binary where the method allows it.**
   - `go`: install only the binaries that are missing/stale (your loop, made conditional).
   - `homebrew`/`curl`: the package ships both together, so a single installer run refreshes both — triggered whenever *either* is stale.
4. **Verify both at the end** (extend the post-install check at `run.go:124-133`).

One design point worth your call before I build it:

content.content:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://goreleaser.com/static/schema-pro.json
version: 2
pro: true

before:
  hooks:
    - go mod tidy
    - mise run completions

builds:
  - id: entire
    main: ./cmd/entire
    binary: entire
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Commit={{.ShortCommit}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry.PostHogAPIKey={{.Env.POSTHOG_API_KEY}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/telemetry.PostHogEndpoint={{.Env.POSTHOG_ENDPOINT}}

  # git-remote-entire is the git remote helper for entire:// URLs (see
  # cmd/git-remote-entire). A small, dedicated binary shipped alongside
  # entire so `git clone entire://…` resolves it on PATH — no telemetry,
  # only the versioninfo stamp it needs for its git agent string.
  - id: git-remote-entire
    main: ./cmd/git-remote-entire
    binary: git-remote-entire
    env:
      - CGO_ENABLED=0
    goos:
      - darwin
      - linux
      - windows
    goarch:
      - amd64
      - arm64
    ldflags:
      - -s -w
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}
      - -X github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo.Commit={{.ShortCommit}}

notarize:
  macos:
    # Must list every darwin build id explicitly. When omitted, goreleaser
    # defaults the id filter to the project name ("cli"), which matched the
    # old single unnamed build but matches neither named build above — the
    # notarize pipe then silently skips and ships ad-hoc-signed binaries that
    # Gatekeeper kills on launch.
    - enabled: '{{ isEnvSet "MACOS_SIGN_P12" }}'
      ids:
        - entire
        - git-remote-entire
      sign:
        certificate: "{{.Env.MACOS_SIGN_P12}}"
        password: "{{.Env.MACOS_SIGN_PASSWORD}}"
      notarize:
        issuer_id: "{{.Env.MACOS_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID}}"
        key_id: "{{.Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY_ID}}"
        key: "{{.Env.MACOS_NOTARY_KEY}}"
        wait: true # do not let an unusable binary slip into the wild

archives:
  - formats:
      - tar.gz
    format_overrides:
      - goos: windows
        formats:
          - zip
    name_template: "entire_{{ .Os }}_{{ .Arch }}"
    files:
      - src: completions/*
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: LICENSE
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"
      - src: README.md
        info:
          owner: root
          group: root
          mtime: "{{ .CommitDate }}"

checksum:
  name_template: "checksums.txt"

release:
  prerelease: auto

scoops:
  - repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: scoop-bucket
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/cli"
    description: "CLI for Entire"
    license: MIT
    skip_upload: auto

homebrew_casks:
  - name: entire
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/cli"
    description: "CLI for Entire"
    binaries:
      - entire
      - git-remote-entire
    generate_completions_from_executable:
      executable: entire
      shell_parameter_format: cobra
      shells:
        - bash
        - zsh
        - fish
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire@nightly
    skip_upload: auto

  - name: entire@nightly
    repository:
      owner: entireio
      name: homebrew-tap
      token: "{{ .Env.TAP_GITHUB_TOKEN }}"
    directory: Casks
    homepage: "https://github.com/entireio/cli"
    description: "CLI for Entire (nightly build)"
    binaries:
      - entire
      - git-remote-entire
    generate_completions_from_executable:
      executable: entire
      shell_parameter_format: cobra
      shells:
        - bash
        - zsh
        - fish
    conflicts:
      - cask: entire
    skip_upload: "{{ if not .Prerelease }}true{{ end }}"

announce:
  discord:
    enabled: '{{ and (not .Prerelease) (isEnvSet "DISCORD_WEBHOOK_ID") (isEnvSet "DISCORD_WEBHOOK_TOKEN") }}'
    message_template: "Beep, boop. **Entire CLI {{ .Tag }}** is out!\n\n{{ .ReleaseURL }}\n\nSee https://docs.entire.io/cli/installation for help installing and updating."
    author: "Entire"

Before I write code across two repos, here's what I found — and one scope decision that's genuinely yours.

## Findings on version baking

- **Release stamping is already correct.** `cli/.goreleaser.yaml` builds `git-remote-entire` as its own build id with the same ldflags as `entire`: `-X .../versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}` and `.Commit={{.ShortCommit}}`. It's also notarized alongside `entire`. So your second ask ("stamp the same version info into git-remote-entire") is **already done** in the release pipeline.
- **The binary already bakes it the same way.** `cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go` calls `versioninfo.Load()` — identical mechanism to `entire` (ldflags wins, build-info `Main.Version` fallback for `go install`).
- **The gap:** `git-remote-entire` *loads* the version but never *exposes* it. It has no `--version` — it's a pure git remote helper (`<remote-name> <url>`, else exit 128). So nothing outside the process can read its version the way `entire --version` works.

## The fork

`entire-upgrade` needs to know `git-remote-entire`'s version to upgrade it independently. Two ways to get it:

The cli repo is on an unrelated branch (`20260603-adjust-login-prompt`, clean) — touching it means a new branch there.

Empirically confirmed — this is the key result:

```
build	-ldflags="-s -w -X .../versioninfo.Version=0.7.4-test -X .../versioninfo.Commit=deadbeef"
```

`go build -ldflags` (exactly what goreleaser runs) records the full ldflags string in the binary's build info, and **`-s -w` does not strip it**. So the release/homebrew binaries *already* carry a readable version in build info — no goreleaser change is actually needed. `entire-upgrade` just has to read it the way the CLI's own `versioninfo.resolve` does: prefer the ldflags `Version=` stamp, fall back to `Main.Version` (which covers the `go install` case, currently `v0.7.3`).

Done. Clean format, all tests pass.

## What was wrong

Your `installWithGo` change was correct — but it never ran. `entire upgrade` decided "already up to date" by comparing **only `entire`'s version**, and `return`ed before `Install` was ever called. Since your `entire` was already at the latest nightly, the helper was never touched. The exact failure you pasted.

## What I changed (all in `entire-upgrade`)

- **Detect the helper independently** (`install.go`): `git-remote-entire` has no `--version` (it's a pure git remote helper), so I read its version from the Go build info baked into the binary — preferring the `-ldflags ...versioninfo.Version=` stamp, falling back to `Main.Version`. This mirrors the CLI's own `versioninfo.resolve` precedence.
- **Gate on both binaries** (`run.go`): "already up to date" now requires `entire` *and* `git-remote-entire` to be current. A missing or stale helper triggers the upgrade even when `entire` is current.
- **Per-binary go install**: the go path now skips any binary already at the target, so a current `entire` isn't needlessly rebuilt — only the helper gets installed.
- **Verify the helper landed**: post-upgrade, hard-fails if `git-remote-entire` is missing beside `entire`; soft-checks its version when readable.
- Tests: ldflags-stamp parsing, and an integration test reproducing your exact case (entire current + helper missing → installs only the helper).

## On your two version-baking asks — already handled, no change needed

- **Release stamping**: `cli/.goreleaser.yaml` already builds `git-remote-entire` as its own build id with `-X ...versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}` and notarizes it alongside `entire`.
- **Reading it uniformly**: I proved that `go build -ldflags` (what goreleaser runs) records the full ldflags string in build info, and `-s -w` doesn't strip it. So Homebrew/install.sh binaries already expose a readable version in build info — which is exactly what the new detection reads. **No goreleaser patch required.**

No commit made — yours to review and push.

Correct — **no changes to `entireio/cli` needed.** Here's the blunt reasoning:

- **Release stamping already covers `git-remote-entire`.** `.goreleaser.yaml` builds it as its own id with `-X ...versioninfo.Version={{.Version}}` + Commit, and notarizes it. Done already.
- **The version is already readable from build info.** I built `git-remote-entire` with the exact goreleaser flags (`-s -w -X ...Version=...`) and confirmed `go build` records the full ldflags string in build info — and `-s -w` doesn't strip it. So Homebrew/install.sh binaries expose their version, and `go install` builds expose `Main.Version`. `entire-upgrade` now reads both.

One caveat worth naming:

- The build-info read depends on the **package path `github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/versioninfo`** staying put. If cli ever relocates the `versioninfo` package, my regex in `entire-upgrade` stops matching the stamp (it'd silently fall back to `Main.Version`, which is unreliable for release binaries). That's a coupling between the two repos, but it lives entirely in `entire-upgrade` — nothing to change in cli today.

The only reason you'd touch cli is if you wanted `git-remote-entire --version` to exist as a first-class feature (so it's inspectable like `entire`, not just via build-info reflection). That's a nicety, not required for the upgrade to work. Want me to add it anyway?

content.text:
Short answer: **no, about half of it is belt-and-suspenders.** The actual bug fix is ~10 lines. The rest is version-parity machinery you asked for — but a lot of it guards a state that can't really happen.

## The load-bearing core (the actual bug)

`entire upgrade` bailed "already up to date" off `entire`'s version alone, so the helper never installed. The minimal fix:
- Gate also fires when `git-remote-entire` is **missing** beside `entire`.
- Install already brings both (your original loop / the brew+curl tarballs).

That's it. ~10 lines + a presence check in verify.

## What's extra, and why it's questionable

The two binaries **ship in lockstep** — same tag, same tarball, always. So "entire current but helper a *different* version" basically can't occur except as a transient broken install. Given that:

| Piece | Lines | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Helper **presence** in gate + verify | ~10 | **Keep** — this is the fix |
| Helper **version** detection (`--version`, `detectHelperVersion`) | ~30 | Optional — only catches *stale-but-present*, which lockstep prevents |
| **ldflags build-info parsing** | ~25 | Weakest — only serves *old release helpers lacking `--version`*, which would self-heal by reinstalling anyway |
| Per-binary **conditional go install** | ~15 | Pure optimization — skips a cheap rebuild |
| `ParseVersion` regex for the helper | ~3 | Cheap; only needed if you keep version detection |

So `git-remote-entire --version` is a fine diagnostic, but it's **not load-bearing** for the upgrade if you trust lockstep. The whole version-comparison path exists to detect drift that the release process doesn't allow.

## Your call

content.text:
Good instinct — that's a cleaner model than what I built. Let me first clarify your question, then redesign.

**"Conditional go install"** = in the `go install` path I skip rebuilding any binary that's already at the target version:
```go
if current.Present && target.Compare(current) == 0 {
    continue   // already current — don't `go install` it again
}
```
So in the "entire current, helper missing" case, only `git-remote-entire` gets built, not `entire`. Without it, every upgrade reruns `go install` on both regardless. It's an optimization, not correctness — and in a per-binary loop it's just one `continue`, so it stops looking like separate "machinery."

## Redesign: one catalog, iterate over it

Replace the entire-special-case + helper-bolt-on with a uniform list. `entire` stays the *discovery anchor* (it's what's on PATH, determines method + dir), but version detection / staleness / install / verify all loop over `{entire, git-remote-entire, …}`. Adding a third binary later = one line in the catalog. The `--version`→build-info logic gets written once and used for all.

Done. Refactored to the per-binary model you wanted — same line count (~163 prod lines vs main), but the structure now earns it.

## What changed structurally

**One catalog drives everything:**
```go
var releaseBinaries = []struct{ Name, GoPkg string }{
    {anchorBinary, "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire"},
    {remoteHelperBinary, "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/git-remote-entire"},
}
```
Adding a third release binary later = one line here. Detection, gating, install, and verify all loop over `install.Binaries`. No more `entire`-special + helper-bolt-on; `entire` is just `Binaries[0]`, distinguished only as the *discovery anchor* (the one on PATH that fixes the dir + install method).

**Version logic written once** — `binaryVersion(ctx, path)`: `--version` → parse → Go build-info fallback. Used for every binary. The only per-binary difference is one line in detection: the anchor's failure is fatal (it's how we found the install), the rest degrade to "absent → reinstall."

**The four call sites are now trivial loops:**
- Gate: `anyBinaryBehind(install, latest)` — missing or older ⇒ upgrade.
- `installWithGo`: `for _, b := range install.Binaries` — skip if already at target, else stage+replace at `b.Path`.
- Verify: `for _, b := range verified.Binaries` — presence mandatory, version enforced when readable.

## On your "treat separately even though lockstep" call
That's baked in now — nothing assumes the two move together. A user with a stale or missing `git-remote-entire` beside a current `entire` gets it fixed independently. The `--version` parity (matching your cli change) and build-info fallback both ride on the shared `binaryVersion`, so old helpers lacking `--version` still resolve via build-info or self-heal via reinstall.

name: upgrade-smoke

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - ".github/workflows/upgrade-smoke.yml"
      - "cmd/entire-upgrade/**"
      - "internal/upgrade/**"
      - "internal/cli/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - ".github/workflows/upgrade-smoke.yml"
      - "cmd/entire-upgrade/**"
      - "internal/upgrade/**"
      - "internal/cli/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  homebrew:
    name: Homebrew install path
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26.2" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Install Entire via Homebrew
        run: |
          brew tap entireio/tap
          for cask in entire entire@nightly; do
            if brew list --cask "$cask" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              brew uninstall --cask "$cask"
            fi
          done
          brew install --cask entire
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        run: |
          ./entire-upgrade | tee stable.log
          grep -F "(homebrew install)" stable.log
          ./entire-upgrade --nightly | tee nightly.log
          grep -F "(homebrew install)" nightly.log
          hash -r
          entire --version

  curl:
    name: install.sh path
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26.2" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Configure isolated HOME
        run: |
          echo "HOME=$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-curl-home" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-curl-home/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Install Entire via install.sh
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          mkdir -p "$HOME"
          curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ENTIRE_UPGRADE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          ./entire-upgrade | tee stable.log
          grep -F "(curl install)" stable.log
          ./entire-upgrade --nightly | tee nightly.log
          grep -F "(curl install)" nightly.log
          entire --version

  go:
    name: go install path
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26.2" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Configure isolated GOBIN
        run: |
          echo "GOBIN=$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-go-bin" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-go-bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Install Entire via go install
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$GOBIN"
          go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@v0.6.1
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          ./entire-upgrade | tee stable.log
          grep -F "(go install)" stable.log
          ./entire-upgrade --nightly | tee nightly.log
          grep -F "(go install)" nightly.log
          entire --version
          test -x "$GOBIN/git-remote-entire"

  go-windows:
    name: go install path (Windows)
    runs-on: windows-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26.2" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade.exe ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Configure isolated GOBIN
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          $goBin = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP "entire-go-bin"
          "GOBIN=$goBin" >> $env:GITHUB_ENV
          $goBin >> $env:GITHUB_PATH
      - name: Install Entire via go install
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $env:GOBIN | Out-Null
          go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@v0.6.1
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        shell: pwsh
        run: |
          .\entire-upgrade.exe | Tee-Object -FilePath stable.log
          if (-not (Select-String -Path stable.log -SimpleMatch "(go install)" -Quiet)) {
            throw "stable upgrade did not detect a go install"
          }
          .\entire-upgrade.exe --nightly | Tee-Object -FilePath nightly.log
          if (-not (Select-String -Path nightly.log -SimpleMatch "(go install)" -Quiet)) {
            throw "nightly upgrade did not detect a go install"
          }
          entire --version
          if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $env:GOBIN "git-remote-entire.exe"))) {
            throw "git-remote-entire was not installed beside entire"
          }

aiTitle: Debug git-remote-entire not upgrading with Entire CLI

content.text:
Root cause is clear and it's in the **workflow, not the code**: none of the smoke jobs pass `--yes`, so `./entire-upgrade` prompts, hits EOF on empty stdin, and aborts. The grep for the detection line still passes (it prints before the prompt), so the homebrew/curl jobs went *vacuously green* — they never actually upgraded. The go jobs added `test -x git-remote-entire`, which is the first assertion that requires the upgrade to truly run, so they're the ones that fail.

Fix: add `--yes` to every invocation so the smoke jobs actually perform the upgrade.

CI pins Go **1.26.2**, but cli `v0.7.3`+ needs **1.26.3**, and `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` blocks the auto-download. Let me find where that go version and `GOTOOLCHAIN` come from:

content.text:
`--yes` was right — now the upgrade actually runs and hits the real issue: `actions/setup-go` pins Go 1.26.2 **and sets `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`**, but `go install`ing the latest cli (`v0.7.3`+) needs Go ≥ 1.26.3. With `local`, Go refuses to auto-fetch the newer toolchain.

The robust fix is `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` for the go-install smoke jobs — the smoke test's whole point is "install the *latest* cli," whose Go floor will keep climbing, so it should fetch whatever toolchain that needs rather than re-pinning on every cli bump. Only the two go jobs `go install` cli (brew/curl don't), so it's scoped there.

          GOTOOLCHAIN: auto
        run: |
          ./entire-upgrade --yes | tee stable.log

      - name: Install Entire via Homebrew
        run: |
          brew tap entireio/tap
          for cask in entire entire@nightly; do
            if brew list --cask "$cask" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              brew uninstall --cask "$cask"
            fi
          done
          brew install --cask entire

        run: |

content.text:
## Why cli needs 1.26.3

`cli/go.mod` line 3 is literally `go 1.26.3` (bumped 2026-05-21, commit `7dcdf91`: "Bump Go to 1.26.3 across mise + lint workflow"). Since Go 1.21, the `go` directive is a **hard minimum** — any toolchain that builds or `go install`s the module must be ≥ that version. So `go install …cli/cmd/entire@v0.7.3` demands ≥1.26.3.

It's not a deep requirement — just a routine patch bump in cli's go.mod. The runner has 1.26.2 + `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (set by `setup-go`), so Go refuses to fetch 1.26.3 and errors instead. `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` lets it fetch — and self-heals on the next cli bump, which is why I prefer it over re-pinning the runner.

Let me commit and push:

Allow toolchain auto-fetch in go-install smoke jobs

`go install`ing the latest cli requires the Go version in its go.mod
(now 1.26.3), which exceeds the runner's pinned 1.26.2. setup-go sets
GOTOOLCHAIN=local, so Go errors instead of fetching it. Set
GOTOOLCHAIN=auto for the two go-install jobs so the smoke test tracks
cli's climbing Go floor without re-pinning the runner each bump.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin upgrade-git-remote-entire 2>&1 | tail -4

content.text:
Confirmed empty. Here's what's going on — **you haven't misunderstood the upgrade; you're looking at a CI result that never included the smoke test.**

## Why PR #4's CI didn't fail

1. **The pushed commit is empty.** `b1abf1d "Empty commit to trigger CI"` has zero file changes vs main. Your no-pin edits to `test.yml` / `upgrade-smoke.yml` are still **uncommitted in your working tree** — they were never pushed to PR #4.

2. **`upgrade-smoke` has a `paths:` filter** (`.github/workflows/upgrade-smoke.yml`, `cmd/entire-upgrade/**`, `internal/**`, `go.mod`, …). An empty commit touches none of them, so the smoke workflow was **skipped — it didn't run, so there was nothing to fail.** The green checks you saw (build / test / lint) don't exercise the upgrade or the `go install` toolchain path at all.

3. **Even once you commit + push the no-pin change, this branch's smoke test would still pass vacuously.** This branch is off main: no `--yes`, no `test -x git-remote-entire`. So `./entire-upgrade` aborts at the `[Y/n]` prompt (EOF on CI stdin) **before it ever reaches `go install`** — the toolchain-version issue can't surface. The grep finds the detection line (printed pre-prompt) and `entire --version` runs on the un-upgraded binary, so it's green while testing nothing.

The `--yes` + helper-presence assertions that actually drive the upgrade — and thus expose both the abort and the 1.26.3 toolchain requirement — only exist on **PR #3 (`upgrade-git-remote-entire`)**.

## Net
- PR #4 (no-pin) **cannot validate itself** with the current smoke test, because the smoke test never performs a real `go install`. The no-pin change only matters *if* the smoke test reaches `go install` — which requires `--yes`.
- So the two PRs are coupled: removing the go pin is only meaningfully testable once the smoke jobs run the upgrade non-interactively.

Want me to (a) bring `--yes` (and `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, or the no-pin approach) onto PR #4 so the smoke test actually runs the upgrade, or (b) fold the no-pin change into PR #3 where the real assertions already live? Your call on how you want these split.

## Next: unpin, separately
I stashed your unpin edits earlier (`git stash` → "wip: unpin golang in CI"). When you're ready, the fix is to let the go-install jobs use a toolchain ≥ cli's floor. Two ways:

- **`GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`** on the go jobs — keeps the pin but lets `go install` fetch whatever cli requires. Self-heals on future cli bumps.

content.text:
Yeah — `actions/setup-go` exports `GOTOOLCHAIN=local` (to pin you to exactly the version it installed), which defeats Go's auto-toolchain. `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto` overrides that and lets `go install` fetch whatever the latest cli requires.

I'll set it at step level on the two go-install Exercise steps (step env reliably overrides the `local` that setup-go injects via `$GITHUB_ENV`). Keeping your `go-version: "1.26"` edit.

## Recap of PR #4

The smoke test went from *vacuously green* → *actually testing the upgrade* → *green for real*:

1. **`--yes` + `pipefail`/`$LASTEXITCODE`** — jobs now run the upgrade non-interactively and a failed upgrade fails the step (no more `tee` swallowing the exit code).
2. **`go-version: "1.26"`** (your edit) — setup-go installs the latest 1.26.x.
3. **`GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`** on the go-install Exercise steps — overrides setup-go's `local` so `go install` fetches whatever toolchain the latest cli requires, instead of dying on the pin.

Net: every install path (Homebrew, install.sh, go install ×2) now genuinely upgrades end-to-end and passes — and it'll keep passing as cli's Go floor climbs, without re-pinning.

PR #4 is green and ready. Note this is the CI-hardening PR; PR #3 (`upgrade-git-remote-entire`) is the separate one carrying the actual git-remote-entire upgrade logic + the `test -x git-remote-entire` assertion — which will benefit from these same `--yes`/`GOTOOLCHAIN` fixes once they land on main or get merged in.

name: upgrade-smoke

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - ".github/workflows/upgrade-smoke.yml"
      - "cmd/entire-upgrade/**"
      - "internal/upgrade/**"
      - "internal/cli/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - ".github/workflows/upgrade-smoke.yml"
      - "cmd/entire-upgrade/**"
      - "internal/upgrade/**"
      - "internal/cli/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  homebrew:
    name: Homebrew install path
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Install Entire via Homebrew
        run: |
          brew tap entireio/tap
          for cask in entire entire@nightly; do
            if brew list --cask "$cask" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              brew uninstall --cask "$cask"
            fi
          done
          brew install --cask entire
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          ./entire-upgrade --yes | tee stable.log
          grep -F "(homebrew install)" stable.log
          ./entire-upgrade --nightly --yes | tee nightly.log
          grep -F "(homebrew install)" nightly.log
          hash -r
          entire --version

  curl:
    name: install.sh path
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Configure isolated HOME
        run: |
          echo "HOME=$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-curl-home" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-curl-home/.local/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Install Entire via install.sh
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          mkdir -p "$HOME"
          curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ENTIRE_UPGRADE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          ./entire-upgrade --yes | tee stable.log
          grep -F "(curl install)" stable.log
          ./entire-upgrade --nightly --yes | tee nightly.log
          grep -F "(curl install)" nightly.log
          entire --version

  go:
    name: go install path
    runs-on: macos-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v6
        with: { go-version: "1.26" }
      - run: go build -o entire-upgrade ./cmd/entire-upgrade
      - name: Configure isolated GOBIN
        run: |
          echo "GOBIN=$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-go-bin" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/entire-go-bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
      - name: Install Entire via go install
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$GOBIN"
          go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@v0.6.1
          entire --version
      - name: Exercise upgrade plugin
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # setup-go exports GOTOOLCHAIN=local; override it so `go install`
          # fetches whatever toolchain the latest cli's go.mod requires.
          GOTOOLCHAIN: auto

Two separate things here, and the second is the real blocker.

## The CI job itself — fixed
The failing Homebrew job was the only upgrade step missing `GITHUB_TOKEN`, so entire-upgrade's release-version check hit GitHub unauthenticated and got a 403 rate-limit. I added `GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}` to that step (matching the curl/go jobs). Committed locally as `21f1d98`.

## But I can't push it — and it's not transient
The `entire://` remote stores the objects, then fails forwarding the push to the GitHub mirror:

```
refs/heads/upgrade-git-remote-entire upstream auth failed:
link your GitHub account at https://entire.io to push to mirror repos:
fetch user github token: github not linked
```

So your entire.io account's **GitHub link is gone/expired** — the server has no GitHub token to mirror the push with. That's an account/auth thing, not something I can fix in code. Earlier pushes this session worked, so it lapsed mid-session.

(Also FYI, unrelated: my own `gh` API calls hit the shared 5,000/hr limit, so I've stopped polling CI.)

## Options to land the fix
1. **Re-link GitHub at https://entire.io** (or whatever `entire login` / re-auth flow applies), then I retry `git push origin` — keeps everything going through the entire mirror as intended.
2. **I add a direct `github.com` remote and push there** to unblock CI now — bypasses the entire mirror, so entire.io would lag GitHub until the link's restored. I won't touch your remotes without you saying so.

Which way do you want to go?

Committed `8cbafe0`. Both your points are handled:

## What changed
- **Unreadable version is no longer fatal.** A local dev `entire` (`--version` → `dev`, build info → `(devel)`) now resolves to *absent*, which the gate already treats as "out of date" → it reinstalls. The anchor is no longer special-cased to hard-fail; it degrades like the helper. So `entire upgrade` on a dev build just does the right thing.
- **The message now says what it tried.** When a version genuinely can't be determined (and surfaces), it reads e.g.:
  > `could not determine entire version: could not parse "entire --version" output "Entire CLI dev"; and reading Go build info from /Users/paul/go/bin/entire did not yield one either`
- **Friendly run-time note** instead of an error:
  > `Detected Entire CLI at /Users/paul/go/bin/entire (go install); could not read its version (a local dev build?), so it will be reinstalled.`
- Dropped the now-dead `versionCommandError` + its test; added a test reproducing your dev-build case (reinstalls, no error).

## To try it on your machine
Rebuild + reinstall the plugin, then rerun:
```
mise build && entire plugin install ./entire-upgrade --force
entire upgrade --nightly --yes
```
Heads up: that will **replace your local dev `entire` with the nightly release** — which is what you asked for, but worth flagging since you build entire from source.
